steps.what: Check database schema versions, notation requirements and the documentation export scope
Render database schemas and dictionaries using the selected accepted notation
Verify notation and explain database schemas, meanings and limitations to colleagues

tasks.design: Generate diagrams and field dictionaries from versioned schema definitions in {DATA_PLATFORM}, using native documentation exports before custom code. Keep meaning, notation checking and colleague explanation with the architect in {DOCS} and discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual transcription and diagram maintenance drift from schema versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalog and definition exports can drive deterministic documentation without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Physical structures do not explain business semantics or undocumented constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what a relationship means and expose where the documented structure is misleading.
tasks.altitude: Maintain documentation definitions and explain architectural meaning instead of redrawing structures.

reach.task: Explain warehouse relationships to a delivery team
reach.learn: How schema notation relates to data use

evidence.claim: Schema definitions and catalogs support deterministic diagram and dictionary generation; compatibility and local savings remain E1.

assumptions: Boundary is documenting and communicating an existing schema, excluding original schema design, data correction and migration. If model rendering is already counted elsewhere, do not count the same rendering here.

Architects and developers produce versioned schema definitions in existing development work before s1. In s1 the focal architect captures exact database/schema version, included objects, fields/types, keys, explicit relationships, notation and exclusions; its 25 hours include export checks and manual reconciliation. No free complete catalog, semantic relationship or export-ready flag is assumed; unsupported constructs are documented manually.
Use native schema export and rendering first. Colleagues supply questions during s3 before the explanation closes; discussion and correction remain retained.
unknowns: Native export coverage and undocumented relationships
research_questions: How much redrawing remains after source version checks and explanation are counted?

tasks.short: Develop data models and describe element use

steps.what: Develop data element meanings, relationships and intended use from business requirements
Render the specified data model and element dictionary using established templates
Check data model semantics, constraints and procedure compliance before accepting the design

tasks.design: Keep semantic modeling with the architect and use native modeling functions in {DATA_PLATFORM} to render an explicit specification and its dictionary. {DOCS} preserves requirements and design decisions; rendering does not choose keys, grain or business meaning.
tasks.previous_blocker: The architect repeats drawing and dictionary formatting after making design choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Modeling tools can render explicit entities, attributes and relationships without a model call.
tasks.still_hard: Business meaning, historical change and conflicting uses require architectural judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Determine whether the model represents the real business rather than merely forming valid tables.
tasks.altitude: Own semantic choices and review model coherence instead of repeatedly formatting them.

reach.task: Clarify controlled definitions and their versions
reach.learn: How to preserve meaning across model revisions

evidence.claim: Explicit model specifications support native diagram and dictionary rendering, while semantic design remains human; local labour shares are E1 estimates.

assumptions: Boundary is developing and representing a data model, excluding schema migration and production execution. Do not count identical rendering again in schema documentation.

Stakeholders supply requirements and explanations before and during s1; existing source owners supply current structures. In s1 the architect captures entities, grain, element definitions, types, keys, cardinalities, optionality, permitted uses and source versions. Its 45 hours include choosing and entering these decisions; no free complete model or approved relationship flag is assumed. Ambiguous cases return to manual modeling.
Test native model templates first. This design changes no production database and transfers no new specification work to stakeholders.
unknowns: Actual rendering share and native modeling support
research_questions: Does native rendering reduce effort after the full semantic specification and consistency checks are counted?

steps.what: Coordinate database development with the project team and determine scope, dependencies and limitations

tasks.design: Retain scope negotiation and dependency discussion with the team. Existing {PROJECT} records and {DOCS} support coordination without treating their status fields as agreements or capacity guarantees.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scope limits depend on trade-offs and commitments across contributors.
tasks.enabler_now: No separate clerical coordination share is established for this task.
tasks.still_hard: Changing requirements and hidden dependencies require discussion and accountable choices.
tasks.human_edge: Expose incompatible expectations and negotiate a feasible boundary.
tasks.altitude: Project coordination and scope judgement retain their time.

reach.learn: How technical constraints change delivery scope

evidence.claim: Database scope coordination requires reciprocal decisions; a project dashboard alone does not establish agreement or local time savings.

assumptions: Boundary is architect participation in coordination and scope determination, excluding project administration and implementation.

The project sponsor supplies objectives before s1 and colleagues supply capacity, limitations and commitments during s1 before scope conclusions. Clarification and existing recording remain retained; no free resource-available or agreed-scope flag exists.

unknowns: Actual decision authority and unresolved dependencies
research_questions: Which recurring scope disputes reflect missing decisions rather than missing status visibility?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Scope negotiation retains its time; no clerical baseline is invented.

tasks.short: Evaluate database industry trends for management

steps.what: Identify relevant database industry sources and capture dated claims with their limitations
Compare database trend claims and draft a source-linked briefing outline

loop.purpose: Organize dated database claims by the architect's questions
loop.input: Verified source packet containing excerpts, versions, dates and limitations
loop.output: Claim comparison linked to packet passages with disagreements retained
loop.check: Architect checks release maturity, benchmark conditions, vendor attribution and every claimed implication; absence of evidence is not agreement.
loop.stop: One comparison and correction pass; unverifiable sections are researched and written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed feeds collect items, but comparing differently worded technical claims requires language interpretation.

steps.what: Evaluate database trends against organizational needs and advise upper management with caveats

tasks.design: Keep source selection and applicability judgement with the architect; use bounded drafting in approved {DOCS} tooling to compare a captured source packet. A native feed or saved search collects source candidates first, and management advice retains explicit uncertainty.
tasks.previous_blocker: Claims from different technical documents take time to align and summarize.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bounded language comparison is plausible without granting production access or autonomous research authority.
tasks.still_hard: Marketing claims and benchmarks may not predict local operational outcomes.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize what would need testing before a trend justifies investment.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time arranging claims and retain source scrutiny and management advice.

reach.task: Discuss evidence behind a database performance claim
reach.learn: How benchmark conditions limit transfer to operational choices

evidence.claim: Source-bounded comparison of technical claims is a plausible drafting use; it does not establish accuracy or measured database-architect savings.

assumptions: Boundary is identifying and evaluating trends and advising management, excluding procurement, migration and local benchmark execution. No actual trend claim is asserted by this design.

Publishers provide documents and management supplies questions before s1. The architect captures document title, publisher, date, version, exact claim passage, benchmark conditions and limitations in s1; its 35 hours include finding and reading sources. No free trusted-source or relevant-trend flag is assumed. Missing sources and contradictory claims remain unresolved and trigger manual research.
Native saved searches and a comparison table come first. Model use is confined to approved source material; no production credentials or agent are needed.
unknowns: Actual source-comparison effort and approved drafting access
research_questions: Does source-bounded comparison reduce effort after finding, reading and checking the underlying claims?

already_counted.description: Source finding, reading and packet capture

incremental.description: Source template checks and failed-comparison follow-up

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=91, gross=9, focal upkeep=6, net=3. Range 0-1 allows difficult source verification, incompatible benchmark conditions and already-efficient comparison notes.
